NoteIn case the same engine is offered for type approval under different constant speed ratings, the type test shall be carried out according to 3.1 for the maximum rated power at the maximum offered speed. The endurance test shall he carried out for the type of IS rating. ( A or B according to IS : 10000 ( Part IX )-1980 for the maximum rating declared. These standards were originally issued in 1960. standards by the manufacturers and testing laboratories, Markin~g Scheme, they have now been extensively revised.

As a result of implementation of these as also the operation of ISI Certification

While IS : 1600 and IS : 1602 covered the codes for type testing of constant and variable speed engines respectively, the performance requireme-nts of such engines were covered by IS : 1601 and lS: 1603 respectively. These standards are replaced by two sets of standards, one sel covers the methods of testing of engines and the other covers the specification and pbrformance requireinents of both constant speed and variable speed engines. The standard covering methods of test is being covering a particular test method or information related IS : 10000 Methods Part.1 Glossary Part II Standard of tests for internal of terms reference relating combustion to test methods published in following to methods of t-ests ): engines: 12 psrts ( each parf

Spark ignition engines for sprayers and similar applications~have been covered by IS : 7347-1974 1Specificatkon for performance requirements of small size spark ignition engines for sprayers `, Two-stroke spark ignition engines for automotive IS : 1603 will be covered by a separate specification. applications which were earlier covered by

This standard, that is, IS : 10002 has been evolved to help the user to quote the power, specific fuel consumption, lubricating oil consumption, etc, for ordering purposes. On the other hand, it This standard would be useful for the manufacturer to declare the performance of his engine. would be mainly applicable for diesel generating sets and other allied fields. The engines for this purpose are expected to be rated for IS Rating A as there is bound to be occasional overloading, For some applications engines may be rated for IS Rating B. In this standard c~ertain preferred power ratings according to R 20 series (and R 20/2, R 20/3, R 20/4, R 2016 derived series ) have been included as it was found that the engines presently manufactured tended to fall in line with this series. It is desirable that the manufacturers declare the power of their engines from one of the preferred values. This standard requires that various classes of engines have the specific fuel consumption While laying down these values the committee has taken cognizance (SFC ) valves as laid down. In view of the need to conserve of the capabilities of the engines manufactumred in India at p,resent. the committee has desired that SFC fuel and to improve the efficiency of diesel engines, values should be improved and has laid down the values that the engines are ex.pected to meet after 1 January 1984. In arriving at these values the committee has envisaged a 5 percent improvement and these values will be further reduced in case there is evidence that this can be done. IS : 10001 and IS : 10002 replace IS : 1601 for diesel engines up to 20 kW and above 20~kW, The category of spark ignition engines for general purposes is not being covered as respectively. these types Of engines are getting extinct due to high fuel costs.
